Thank you for writing to us again. We understand this is your sixth time raising this concern, and we are sorry it has taken this long. You have told us that certain accounts on your credit report resulted from identity theft or fraud, and that you did not receive any goods, services or money from them.

If you have already sent these, please tell us when, so we can locate them. If you have not, please send them, and we will review the accounts you have identified.

We will also reinvestigate your dispute under FCRA section 611, generally within 30 days. If we find that information is inaccurate or cannot be verified, we will delete or correct it. We will send you written results within 5 business days after the investigation ends.

If you have questions, please reply with your full name, contact details and the account names or numbers you dispute.

Thank you for contacting us about the hold on your Apple Card account. We understand that you made several payments totaling about $1,950, that your balance updated right away, and that a hold of up to 7 to 14 business days has since been placed on the account. We will review the reason for the hold, check whether it matches the terms of your cardholder agreement, and confirm that each of your payments was applied correctly. Under the Truth in Lending Act and its rules (Regulation Z), a credit card payment must be credited as of the date it is received. We will check that this was followed on your account.

Sincerely,
Goldman Sachs Bank USA Complaints Team

reply:
Dear Customer,

Thank you for writing about the $9,200 charge on your Home Depot account that you say you did not make. We understand how upsetting this is, and we are sorry for the stress it has caused.

Your case is being reviewed by a team member. We will look at the concerns you raised, including how the charge was approved, how the Account Lookup feature works, and the way we verify your identity. We will also review whether other verification options are available to you, and we will tell you the outcome in writing.

Under federal billing error rules (Regulation Z, the Fair Credit Billing Act), we must acknowledge your dispute in writing within 30 days and resolve it within two billing cycles, and no later than 90 days. While your dispute is open, we cannot collect the disputed amount or report it as past due. Federal law also generally limits your liability for unauthorized credit card use to $50.

We will send you a written answer with our findings and the reasons for them, as far as the rules allow. Please keep copies of all letters you receive, and tell us right away about any other charges you do not recognize.

Sincerely,
Citibank Customer Care

Address the consumer's objection to mailing or faxing a driver's license copy more directly, for example by saying the team will explain which verification options are available and why. The draft only says verification options will be reviewed.
Replace 'as far as the rules allow' with a plainer statement of what the consumer will receive and when, since the consumer has already said they cannot get details of the findings.

Consider naming the specific dispute route (a billing error notice under 12 CFR 1026.13) so the consumer can see which process applies, and state that the 60-day notice window is already met, since the consumer disputed promptly.

Consider a short line on the consumer's other questions (why the transaction was approved and how Account Lookup works), with a clear next step or contact for those answers, so they are not left unanswered in the first reply.

Under Regulation E (12 CFR 1005.2(m)), a transfer the consumer was tricked into making is generally not an unauthorized transfer, and the search returned no rule requiring a refund for a correctly processed transfer. The remittance rule does allow error reports within 180 days, so the reply points the consumer to that route without promising a refund. PayPal's history shows 61.4% of past complaints closed with explanation only, and this case has no clear error or unauthorized access to correct. Escalation is not needed: the fraud risk flag is handled by a separate rule, and the consumer faces no serious harm within days.
reply:
Dear Consumer,

Thank you for telling us about the $3,000.00 transfer you sent through Xoom. We are sorry for the distress this has caused, and we understand why you feel uneasy.

You sent this money to a person you now believe scammed you, and you have not heard from them since. We have reviewed your refund request. The transfer was processed as you instructed, so we cannot reverse it on that basis alone. Federal remittance rules under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act give you the right to report an error on an international transfer within 180 days of the transfer. If you believe an error occurred, such as the money not reaching the intended recipient, please reply with the transfer details. We must investigate any reported error within 90 days and will tell you the result in writing.

To protect your PayPal account, please change your password, turn on two-step verification, and never share verification codes with anyone who contacts you. We also recommend reporting this scam to the Federal Trade Commission at ReportFraud.ftc.gov and to your local police. If you have questions about the check you asked for, please contact your bank.

Sincerely,
PayPal Customer Support

Replace 'We have reviewed your refund request' with wording that matches the stage of the case, such as 'We have received your refund request and will look into it.' The investigation has not been completed, so a review claim may overstate what has happened.

The line 'If you have questions about the check you asked for, please contact your bank' may confuse the consumer, because any refund payment would come from the company. Consider removing it or explaining who issues the check and how the consumer will be told the outcome.
Consider a clearer 'what happens next' sentence, such as the consumer can expect a written result from the investigation team, with no dates given.

We understand you are concerned that payments made on your account by a family member, including Federal Reserve Notes, are being credited improperly. We also understand that you sent a tender and a letter of instructions to Ocwen headquarters by registered mail.

Under the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (RESPA), Regulation X, a mortgage servicer must acknowledge a written notice of error within 5 business days. We will review your letter of instructions and the tender you sent, along with how payments on your account have been credited, under this process.

Dear Consumer,

Thank you for explaining how being unemployed while studying for the bar exam affected your Discover account. We understand how stressful it is to see four delinquency notices on your credit report, even though your co-signers paid the past-due amount and you have since enrolled in a payment plan.

Our team will look into how Discover reported each of the delinquencies on your credit report, including the delinquency for XXXX that you described. You told us it was reported even though you had not made a payment yet and were already enrolled in a plan. We will explain our findings to you.

The Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) gives you the right to dispute information on your credit report that you believe is inaccurate. If you send a written dispute to the credit bureau reporting the information, the bureau must investigate, generally within 30 days, and must delete or correct anything it cannot verify. To help us, please send any payment plan confirmation and records of the co-signers' payment that you have.

Thank you for your patience.

Dear Customer,

Thank you for contacting us about your mortgage application, which we denied on XX/XX/2023 based in part on information in a consumer report. We understand this is frustrating, and we take your privacy concerns seriously. We will review the reasons for the decision and how the consumer report was obtained and used in your application.

Under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, a lender must give an applicant a written notice that states the specific reasons for a denial, or tells the applicant how to request those reasons. If you have not received that notice, please tell us and we will provide the reasons.

The Fair Credit Reporting Act also gives you rights. You can request a free copy of your consumer report, and if you believe any information in it is inaccurate, you can dispute it with the credit bureau.

Your complaint also mentions securities fraud and breach of contract. This complaints process cannot decide legal claims, so if you want to pursue them, you may wish to speak with an attorney.

We will send you a written response once our review is complete. Please reply with any documents or details you would like us to consider.

reply:
Dear Customer,

We are sorry to hear about your husband's illness and the strain this is putting on your family. We understand you say you never received or activated the card, that $880 in charges were made on it, and that you filed a police report (report number XXXX), which is in your file.

Your fraud dispute is being reviewed, including the police report you provided. Our written response will address your three questions about the phone number used to activate the card, whether the person knew your Social Security number, and whether a photo of the person making the charges exists.

While your dispute is open, the law does not allow us to collect the disputed $880 or report it as past due. Under the Fair Credit Billing Act, part of Regulation Z (12 CFR 1026.13), we must resolve a billing dispute within two billing cycles and no later than 90 days after we receive your written notice. Federal law also limits your liability for unauthorized credit card use to $50 (12 CFR 1026.12(b)).

We will write to you with our findings and the reasons for our decision. If you have more documents to support your claim, please send them to us in writing and include your account number.

Say plainly that the written response will answer the three specific questions (activation phone number, whether the person knew the SSN, and whether a photo exists) and, where the company cannot share a detail, say so and why. Do not promise that any particular answer will be given.
Briefly acknowledge the second theft and the concern that the system does not protect vulnerable customers, without admitting fault or promising outcomes.
Clarify that the $50 liability cap is a general federal limit and does not decide this dispute, so the consumer does not read it as a statement that they owe $50.
Add a direct contact route (phone number or secure message option and a reference to the account) and mention that the consumer can ask for a status update at any time.
Consider noting that the company will acknowledge the written dispute in writing, which the consumer can check against the 30-day acknowledgment rule, without stating a specific date.

Dear Customer,

We are sorry to hear that your monthly mortgage payment roughly doubled after your loan was transferred to Chase, and that court and eviction proceedings followed. We understand how stressful this has been, especially after about 25 years in your home.

We will look into this concern. The Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (RESPA) gives you the right to dispute your mortgage account in writing. We will review how your payment amount was set after the servicing transfer, including your payment history and any escrow changes.

To start this review, please send us a written notice of error with your loan number, a copy of your latest mortgage statement, and a short explanation of the amount you believe is wrong. Once we receive it, we will acknowledge it within 5 business days. Generally within 30 business days, we will tell you in writing whether we found an error and corrected it, or why we believe the amount is correct. We will also check the status of the court and eviction actions connected to your account and let you know what we find.

If you have questions in the meantime, please call the number on your statement.

Sincerely,
Chase Customer Care

consumer_request: The complaint does not state an explicit request. The implied request is for Wells Fargo to investigate the scam transfers and help recover or reimburse the lost funds.
outcome_reasoning: The consumer says they were tricked into sending money to a romance-investment scam. Under Regulation E (12 CFR 1005.2(m)), a transfer the consumer was tricked into making is generally not an unauthorized transfer, so a fraud-victim claim is not likely to produce a refund under the EFTA error process. The company's history shows 81.4% of past complaints closed with an explanation only, versus 9.5% with monetary relief. The reply therefore explains the review and what documents to keep, without promising money. The review is still open, so the reply does not pre-judge it. Escalation is not needed: the harm is financial but there is no scheduled foreclosure, repossession, or loss of money needed for living costs being held, and the fraud and hardship flags do not by themselves require a person to decide.
reply:
Dear Customer,

We are very sorry for what you have been through. Being targeted by a romance investment scam is painful, and we understand that it has left you with loan payments and a second job you did not plan for.

We are reviewing the transfers you made from your Wells Fargo account to the intermediary and then to the company you named. This review will determine which rules apply to these transfers. The Electronic Fund Transfer Act and its rule, Regulation E, may apply depending on how the transfers were sent. The review will also consider what options may be available to you. We will write to you with what we find and any options that apply, and we will contact you if we need more information.

We know this does not undo your losses. Please keep all messages, receipts, transfer records and loan statements. These can help with your case and with any report you make to other authorities. For questions about your loan payments, please contact your lender directly.

Thank you for telling us what happened. If you have more information, please reply to this message.
critic_suggestions: Consider stating plainly that Regulation E generally covers unauthorized transfers, and that transfers the consumer was tricked into making themselves are often not treated as unauthorized. The current 'may apply depending on how the transfers were sent' wording is accurate but leaves the consumer unsure where they stand.
Consider saying what the consumer can expect next, such as roughly how the company will contact them and that they can add information at any time, so the next step is easier to follow.
Consider acknowledging the consumer's request directly, for example that they asked for help recovering the lost funds, so the reply visibly addresses the main request.
The reply does not mention the consumer's right to ask for the investigation to be reviewed or to contact the company again. Adding this would be helpful but is not required.

reply:
Dear Consumer,

Thank you for contacting us about the entries on your credit report for your vehicle loan. We understand how stressful this has been, especially after you asked us to pick up the car during a difficult health period.

We are reviewing your dispute, including the late-payment and open-status entries. We will check our account records and the information you have provided about the vehicle's return, and we will confirm what should be reported to the credit bureaus.

Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, when a credit bureau receives a dispute, it must generally reinvestigate within 30 days, or up to 45 days if you send more information during that time. A company that reports information to the bureaus, such as Credit Acceptance, must also investigate disputes the bureau forwards and correct any information it finds to be inaccurate. You will receive written results of the investigation.

If you have any additional documents, such as the surrender or return paperwork, please send them to us so we can include them in the review.

Sincerely,
Credit Acceptance Complaints Team
critic_suggestions: Replace the generic 'Dear Consumer' salutation with the consumer's name if it is on file.

Make clear that the 30/45-day reinvestigation timeline is the credit bureau's obligation and applies when the dispute reaches the bureau. Credit Acceptance's own duty is to investigate forwarded disputes and correct inaccurate data. The consumer could read the current wording as a timeline Credit Acceptance is committing to for this dispute.

Where the furnisher duty is described, add that corrections must be made with every credit bureau the company reported to, as Sec. 623(b) requires. This matches the consumer's citation of 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2.
Consider briefly acknowledging the other sections the consumer cited (1681 and 1681a) without debating them, so the consumer sees all their points were read.
Optionally mention that the consumer may request a free report from each nationwide bureau once every 12 months (Sec. 612) so they can check how the entries currently appear.

Dear Customer,

Thank you for explaining your situation in such detail. We understand that you picked up your Tesla in New Jersey while living in Maine, that your 30-day temporary plate has expired, and that you have not received your registration packet or permanent plates. We also understand that you paid the sales or use taxes and registration fees up front, and that you cannot legally drive the vehicle right now. Our team will confirm what has been sent to the New Jersey location and to the Maine registration office, check where your registration packet and plates stand, and review whether another temporary plate can be issued while this is resolved. We will send you a written status update that explains what we found and the next steps, including who is responsible for each one.

Your complaint is being handled through our standard complaints process, and a member of our team will contact you with that update. If you have any new information in the meantime, such as a tracking number or a message from the Maine office, please send it so we can include it in our review.

Sincerely,
Tesla Customer Care

Acknowledge that the consumer's texts have gone unanswered for several hours and that the previous update promised by phone was not delivered. This would address the frustration without admitting fault.

Consider stating when the consumer can expect the written status update, without committing to an outcome. The reply currently gives no timeframe, which the consumer may find vague given the expired plate.

We are sorry for the frustration you have experienced with your debt management program and with the late reporting on your three credit cards. Dear Customer,

Thank you for writing to us. We understand how upsetting it is to find your gift card drained after you had saved it for an emergency, especially when you say you never visited the merchant and never shared your card details. We are sorry for the distress this has caused.

Your complaint raises a fair question about the timeframe we applied when we denied your dispute. We will review your reported transactions again, including the timing of your report and the evidence you provided, under the electronic fund transfer error resolution rules that protect prepaid card holders (the Electronic Fund Transfer Act and Regulation E). If you have additional information, such as any records of your card use or where and when you last used the card, please send it to us so it can be included in the review. We will also make sure your questions about the earlier denial are answered directly.

Sincerely,
InComm Customer Complaints Team

Dear Consumer,

Thank you for explaining your concern. You say that Phoenix Financial Services paid off small medical collections about two years ago in one lump sum, that Phoenix reported the full amount to your credit report about six months ago, that you asked for billing details and did not receive them, and that the debt was later sold to another company as a new debt, even though you believe the account is more than seven years old.

We are looking into each of these points. We will check the payment history, the date the account first became past due, what was reported to the credit bureaus, and whether the debt sale was recorded correctly.

The Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) protects your right to accurate information on your credit report. If you dispute an item with a credit bureau, the bureau must generally complete a reinvestigation within 30 days, or up to 45 days if you send more information during that time. Information that is inaccurate, outdated, or cannot be verified must be corrected or removed. Under the FCRA, most negative items must generally come off a credit report after seven years.

We will write to you with our findings and any action we take. If you have proof of payment or letters showing the date of the first missed payment, please send them to us so we can finish the review faster.

Dear Consumer,

Thank you for contacting us. We understand that you dispute owing this credit card debt, that you never received notice of it, and that you believe interest is being collected on an account that should have been charged off and closed. We take these concerns seriously and will review the account, your dispute, and the records we hold for this debt.

Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (FDCPA), a debt collector must send a validation notice that states the amount owed and the name of the creditor. If you dispute the debt in writing within 30 days after receiving that notice, the collector must stop collection until it mails you verification of the debt. The FDCPA also prohibits collectors from making false or misleading statements about the amount or status of a debt, and from collecting amounts that are not authorized by the agreement or by law. As part of our review, we will check whether the interest being collected is permitted under the account terms and applicable law.

We will send you a written response once our review is complete. If you have any documents you received about this account, or details about when you first learned of it, please send them to us so we can include them in our review.

Sincerely,
Complaints Team
